Loading the datasets¶

dataset_path = kagglehub.dataset_download("ealtman2019/credit-card-transactions")

file_path_cards = os.path.join(dataset_path, 'sd254_cards.csv')
file_path_users = os.path.join(dataset_path, 'sd254_users.csv')

Preparation¶

Converting column headers to lowercase, replacing spaces with underscores, removing symbols, and converting data into a numeric format.

In [5]:
users = users.reset_index().rename(columns={'index': 'user'})
In [6]:
users = users.copy()
# change columns name
users.columns = (
    users.columns
    .str.strip()
    .str.lower()
    .str.replace(' ', '_')
    .str.replace('-', '_')
)
users = users.rename(columns={'per_capita_income___zipcode': 'per_capita_income_zipcode', 'yearly_income___person': 'yearly_income_person'})


# remove $ from money columns
money_cols = ['per_capita_income_zipcode', 'yearly_income_person', 'total_debt']

for col in money_cols:
    users[col] = (
        users[col]
        .astype(str)
        .str.replace('$', '', regex=False)
        .str.replace(',', '', regex=False)
    )
    users[col] = pd.to_numeric(users[col], errors='coerce')

User Demographics¶

Demographics Summary¶

In [14]:
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter

# 1. DATA PREPARATION
user_demographics = [
    'user', 'gender', 'current_age', 'yearly_income_person', 
    'total_debt', 'fico_score', 'num_credit_cards'
]

# Assuming 'df' is defined previously
users_df = df[user_demographics].drop_duplicates(subset=['user']).copy()

print(f"Total Unique Users Analyzed: {len(users_df):,}")
print("\n--- Summary Statistics of the Population ---")
print(users_df.describe().round(1).to_string())

# 2. PREPARE POPULATION PYRAMID DATA
bins = range(10, 105, 5)
labels = [f'{i}-{i+4}' for i in bins[:-1]]
users_df['age_group'] = pd.cut(users_df['current_age'], bins=bins, labels=labels, right=False)

# OPTIMIZATION: pd.crosstab is cleaner for frequency tables than groupby.size.unstack
pyramid_data = pd.crosstab(users_df['age_group'], users_df['gender']).reset_index()

has_standard_genders = 'Female' in pyramid_data.columns and 'Male' in pyramid_data.columns
if has_standard_genders:
    pyramid_data['Female_Plot'] = -pyramid_data['Female']

# 3. VISUALIZATIONS: Demographic Dashboard
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(18, 10))
fig.suptitle('Demographics', fontsize=20, y=0.95)

# --- Plot 1: Gender Distribution ---
gender_counts = users_df['gender'].value_counts()
axes[0, 0].pie(gender_counts, labels=gender_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=['#4c72b0', '#c44e52'])
axes[0, 0].set_title('Gender Distribution', fontsize=14)

# --- Plot 2: Population Pyramid ---
if has_standard_genders:
    sns.barplot(data=pyramid_data, y='age_group', x='Male', color='#4c72b0', label='Male', ax=axes[0, 1])
    sns.barplot(data=pyramid_data, y='age_group', x='Female_Plot', color='#c44e52', label='Female', ax=axes[0, 1])
    
    axes[0, 1].set(title='Population Pyramid: Age & Gender', xlabel='Number of Users', ylabel='Age Group')
    axes[0, 1].invert_yaxis()
    
    # OPTIMIZATION: Use FuncFormatter to avoid UserWarnings when setting tick labels
    axes[0, 1].xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda x, pos: f"{int(abs(x))}"))
    axes[0, 1].axvline(0, color='black', linewidth=1)
    axes[0, 1].legend(title='Gender', loc='upper right')
else:
    axes[0, 1].text(0.5, 0.5, 'Standard Male/Female\nData Not Found', ha='center', va='center')
    axes[0, 1].set_title('Population Pyramid', fontsize=14)

# --- Plots 3, 4, 5: Histograms (OPTIMIZATION: DRY Principle via loop) ---
hist_configs = [
    ('fico_score', 20, 'green', 'FICO Score Distribution', 'FICO Score', axes[0, 2]),
    ('yearly_income_person', 30, 'teal', 'Yearly Income Distribution', 'Yearly Income ($)', axes[1, 0]),
    ('total_debt', 30, 'darkred', 'Total Debt Distribution', 'Total Debt ($)', axes[1, 1])
]

for col, hist_bins, color, title, xlabel, ax in hist_configs:
    sns.histplot(data=users_df, x=col, bins=hist_bins, kde=True, color=color, ax=ax)
    ax.set(title=title, xlabel=xlabel, ylabel='Number of Users')

# --- Plot 6: Credit Cards ---
# OPTIMIZATION: Added hue to match x and legend=False to avoid Seaborn deprecation warnings
sns.countplot(data=users_df, x='num_credit_cards', hue='num_credit_cards', palette='viridis', legend=False, ax=axes[1, 2])
axes[1, 2].set(title='Number of Credit Cards Owned', xlabel='Number of Cards', ylabel='Number of Users')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.subplots_adjust(top=0.88) 
plt.show()

Age and fraud transations¶

In [15]:
# 1. Define your age bins and labels
age_bins = [0, 18, 26, 36, 46, 56, 66, 120]
age_labels = ['<18', '18-25', '26-35', '36-45', '46-55', '56-65', '65+']

# 2. Create the 'age_group' column on the ENTIRE dataframe
df['age_group'] = pd.cut(df['current_age'], 
                         bins=age_bins, 
                         labels=age_labels, 
                         right=False)

# 3. Calculate the fraud rate
fraud_rates = df.groupby('age_group', observed=False)['is_fraud'].mean() * 100

fraud_rates_df = fraud_rates.reset_index()
fraud_rates_df.rename(columns={'is_fraud': 'fraud_rate_pct'}, inplace=True)

# 4. Set up and generate the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Use a bar plot to show the calculated rates
sns.barplot(data=fraud_rates_df, x='age_group', y='fraud_rate_pct', color='teal')

plt.title('Fraud Rate (%) by Age Group', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Age Group', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Fraud Rate (%)', fontsize=14)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Payment Method¶

In [16]:
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# 1. Macro Trend: Transaction Methods by Year
year_chip_crosstab = pd.crosstab(df['year'], df['use_chip'])

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
ax1 = sns.lineplot(data=year_chip_crosstab, markers=True, dashes=False, linewidth=2.5, palette="pastel")

# Optimized: Streamlined axis labeling
ax1.set(title='Evolution of Transaction Methods Over the Years', xlabel='Year', ylabel='Number of Transactions')
plt.legend(title='Transaction Method', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 2. Proportion Trend: 100% Stacked Area Chart
year_chip_pct = year_chip_crosstab.div(year_chip_crosstab.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100

# Optimized: Removed unused palette variables and reverted to pandas .plot.area() 
# as it handles transpositions and legends automatically, keeping the code DRY.
ax2 = year_chip_pct.plot.area(figsize=(12, 6), color=sns.color_palette('pastel'), alpha=0.8)

ax2.set(title='Market Share of Transaction Methods by Year', xlabel='Year', ylabel='Percentage of Transactions (%)')
plt.legend(title='Transaction Method', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.margins(x=0, y=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
In [17]:
method_stats = df.groupby('use_chip').agg(
    Total_Transactions=('is_fraud', 'count'),
    Fraud_Count=('is_fraud', 'sum')
).reset_index()

method_stats['Fraud_Rate_Within_Method (%)'] = (method_stats['Fraud_Count'] / method_stats['Total_Transactions']) * 100
method_stats['Share_of_Total_Fraud (%)'] = (method_stats['Fraud_Count'] / method_stats['Fraud_Count'].sum()) * 100

print("--- Fraud Statistics by Transaction Method ---")
print(method_stats[['use_chip', 'Fraud_Rate_Within_Method (%)', 'Share_of_Total_Fraud (%)']].to_string(index=False))

# Visualization 1: Pie Chart
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.pie(
    method_stats['Share_of_Total_Fraud (%)'],
    labels=method_stats['use_chip'],
    autopct='%1.1f%%',
    startangle=140,
    explode=[0.03] * len(method_stats),
    colors=sns.color_palette('pastel')
)
plt.title('Share of Total Fraud by Method (1991 - 2020)', fontsize=16)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 1. Create the is_online helper column
df['is_online'] = df['merchant_city'] == 'ONLINE'

# 2. Calculate Fraud Rate (%) per Category
online_fraud_stats = df.groupby('is_online')['is_fraud'].value_counts(normalize=True).unstack() * 100

# Rename columns for clarity (True/False to Valid/Fraud)
online_fraud_stats.columns = ['Valid (%)', 'Fraud (%)']
online_fraud_stats.index = ['In-Person', 'Online']

print("Fraud Rate (%) - Online vs. In-Person:")
print(online_fraud_stats)

# 3. Calculate the share of total fraud (Fixed the 'Yes' to True)
total_fraud = df[df['is_fraud'] == True]

if len(total_fraud) > 0:
    percent_fraud_is_online = (total_fraud['is_online'].sum() / len(total_fraud)) * 100
    print(f"\nPercentage of all fraud that happens online: {percent_fraud_is_online:.2f}%")
else:
    print("\nNo fraudulent transactions found. Check if the 'is_fraud' column contains boolean True values.")

Merchant and Fraud¶

Check which stores have the most credit card fraud.

In [20]:
# 1. Convert 'Yes'/'No' strings to Boolean True/False
transactions_mcc['is_fraud'] = transactions_mcc['is_fraud'].map({'Yes': True, 'No': False})

# 2. Calculate fraud stats per merchant category (IRS Description)
# We filter for categories with more than 1,000 transactions to ensure statistical significance
mcc_analysis = transactions_mcc.groupby('irs_description')['is_fraud'].agg(['count', 'mean'])
mcc_analysis.columns = ['Total Transactions', 'Fraud Rate']

# 3. Filter for significant volume to avoid outliers (e.g., a category with 1 transaction that is fraud)
significant_mcc = mcc_analysis[mcc_analysis['Total Transactions'] > 1000]

Geographic and Fraud¶

Which states and city has the most fraud

In [23]:
# Filter for only fraudulent transactions
fraud_df = df[df['is_fraud'] == True].copy()

# Set up the matplotlib figure
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 6))
fig.suptitle('Geographical Distribution of Fraudulent Transactions', fontsize=18, y=1.02)

# --- Plot 1: Top 10 States for Fraud ---
top_states = fraud_df['merchant_state'].value_counts().head(10)

sns.barplot(
    x=top_states.values, 
    y=top_states.index, 
    hue=top_states.index,
    palette='Reds_r', 
    ax=axes[0],
    legend=False
)
axes[0].set_title('Merchant States with Most Fraud', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Number of Fraudulent Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Merchant State', fontsize=12)

# --- Plot 2: Top 10 Cities for Fraud ---
top_cities = fraud_df['merchant_city'].value_counts().head(10)

sns.barplot(
    x=top_cities.values, 
    y=top_cities.index, 
    hue=top_cities.index,
    palette='Oranges_r', 
    ax=axes[1],
    legend=False
)
axes[1].set_title('Merchant Cities with Most Fraud', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Number of Fraudulent Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Merchant City', fontsize=12)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# ==========================================
# 1. DATA PREPARATION
# ==========================================

# Filter for only fraudulent transactions for the count plots
fraud_df = df[df['is_fraud'] == True].copy()
fraud_df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(fraud_df[['year', 'month', 'day']])
fraud_df['day_of_week'] = fraud_df['date'].dt.day_name()

# Aggregate data for the Seasonal Dual-Axis plot (using full df for rate)
seasonal_stats = df.groupby('month')['is_fraud'].agg(
    Total_Transactions='count',
    Fraud_Count='sum'
).reset_index()
seasonal_stats['Fraud_Rate (%)'] = (seasonal_stats['Fraud_Count'] / seasonal_stats['Total_Transactions']) * 100
seasonal_stats['Month_Name'] = seasonal_stats['month'].apply(lambda x: calendar.month_abbr[x])

# ==========================================
# 2. DASHBOARD SETUP
# ==========================================
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(18, 14))
fig.suptitle('Comprehensive Fraudulent Transactions Analysis', fontsize=22, weight='bold', y=1.02)

# Define shared orders
dow_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
month_order = [calendar.month_abbr[i] for i in range(1, 13)]

# --- Plot A: Fraud by Year (Top Left) ---
sns.countplot(data=fraud_df, x='year', ax=axes[0, 0], color='crimson')
axes[0, 0].set_title('A. Fraud Volume by Year', fontsize=14, weight='semibold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Year')
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Total Fraud Count')

axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# --- Plot B: Seasonal Effects (Top Right) ---
ax_vol = axes[0, 1]

# 1. Bar Chart for Volume
sns.barplot(
    data=seasonal_stats, 
    x='Month_Name', 
    y='Fraud_Count', 
    order=month_order,
    color='lightcoral', 
    alpha=0.8, 
    ax=ax_vol,
    label='Fraud Count'
)

# Widen Volume Y-axis: Get max value and add 15% headroom
vol_max = seasonal_stats['Fraud_Count'].max()
ax_vol.set_ylim(0, vol_max * 1.15) 

ax_vol.set_ylabel('Total Fraudulent Transactions', color='darkred', fontsize=12)
ax_vol.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='darkred')
ax_vol.set_title('B. Seasonal Effects: Volume vs. Rate', fontsize=14, weight='semibold')

# 2. Create the twin axis for the Rate
ax_rate = ax_vol.twinx()
sns.lineplot(
    data=seasonal_stats, 
    x='Month_Name', 
    y='Fraud_Rate (%)', 
    color='black', 
    marker='o', 
    linewidth=2.5, 
    ax=ax_rate,
    label='Fraud Rate (%)'
)

# Widen Rate Y-axis: Get max rate and add 15% headroom
rate_max = seasonal_stats['Fraud_Rate (%)'].max()
ax_rate.set_ylim(0, rate_max * 1.15) 

ax_rate.set_ylabel('Fraud Rate (%)', color='black', fontsize=12)
ax_rate.grid(False)

# --- Plot C: Fraud by Day of the Month (Bottom Left) ---
sns.countplot(data=fraud_df, x='day', ax=axes[1, 0], color='darkorange')
axes[1, 0].set_title('C. Fraud Volume by Day of Month', fontsize=14, weight='semibold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Day of Month')

# --- Plot D: Fraud by Day of the Week (Bottom Right) ---
sns.countplot(data=fraud_df, x='day_of_week', order=dow_order, ax=axes[1, 1], color='gold')
axes[1, 1].set_title('D. Fraud Volume by Day of Week', fontsize=14, weight='semibold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Day of Week')

# Final Adjustments
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 1. Filter only fraud rows immediately
fraud_df = df[df['is_fraud'] == True].copy()

# 2. Extract Hour and Day of Week
# Assuming 'time' is in HH:MM format
fraud_df['hour'] = pd.to_datetime(fraud_df['time'], format='%H:%M').dt.hour

# Combine year, month, and day into a datetime object to get the day name
fraud_df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(fraud_df[['year', 'month', 'day']])
fraud_df['day_of_week'] = fraud_df['date'].dt.day_name()

# 3. Aggregate data for the heatmap
# We count the number of occurrences for each hour/day combination
heatmap_data = fraud_df.groupby(['day_of_week', 'hour']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

# 4. Reorder days to ensure the plot reads Monday -> Sunday
days_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
heatmap_data = heatmap_data.reindex(days_order)

# 5. Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 7))
sns.heatmap(heatmap_data, cmap='YlOrRd', linewidths=.5)

plt.title('When do Fraudsters Strike? (Total Fraudulent Transactions)', fontsize=15)
plt.xlabel('Hour of the Day', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Day of the Week', fontsize=12)

# 1. Filter only fraud rows
fraud_df = df[df['is_fraud'] == True].copy()

# 2. Extract Hour and Day of Week
fraud_df['hour'] = pd.to_datetime(fraud_df['time'], format='%H:%M').dt.hour
fraud_df['day_of_week'] = pd.to_datetime(fraud_df[['year', 'month', 'day']]).dt.day_name()

# 3. Aggregate data for the line plot (Frequency per Hour per Day)
days_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
hourly_day_counts = fraud_df.groupby(['day_of_week', 'hour']).size().reindex(
    pd.MultiIndex.from_product([days_order, range(24)], names=['day_of_week', 'hour']), 
    fill_value=0
).reset_index(name='count')

# 4. Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))
sns.lineplot(data=hourly_day_counts, x='hour', y='count', hue='day_of_week', 
             hue_order=days_order, palette='viridis', linewidth=2, marker='o')

# 5. Adding a background sine wave to show the theoretical daily period
x = np.linspace(0, 23, 100)
y_period = (np.sin(2 * np.pi * x / 24 - np.pi/2) + 1) * (hourly_day_counts['count'].max() / 2)
plt.plot(x, y_period, color='black', linestyle='--', alpha=0.2, label='Theoretical Daily Wave')

plt.title('Daily Fraud Cycles: Hourly Trends by Day of Week', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Hour of the Day', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Fraud Count', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(range(0, 24))
plt.legend(title='Day of Week', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.grid(True, linestyle=':', alpha=0.5)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

fraud = df[df['is_fraud'] == True].copy()
